name: sol_heuristics_11
description: Uninitialized state variable confused with a valid default value used as initialization check
question: The source file in `source` uses a state variable's default value (such as zero, empty address, or empty string) as the sole signal that the contract or a struct/mapping entry is uninitialized, even though that same default is also a legitimate valid value the variable could hold after proper initialization, so code paths cannot distinguish an uninitialized state from a genuinely valid zero/empty state, enabling logic bypass or incorrect access-control decisions. This excludes cases where a dedicated boolean flag, explicit initializer-only modifier, or sentinel value distinct from all valid values is used to track initialization.
criteria: A function checks `if (owner == address(0))` to decide whether to run one-time initialization logic, but address(0) could also be intentionally set later as a valid owner value
A struct field defaulting to 0 is checked as `if (config.threshold == 0) revert NotInitialized()` even though 0 is an allowed valid threshold value elsewhere in the contract
A mapping value is checked with `if (balances[user] == 0)` to infer that a user record has never been set, while 0 is also a legitimate balance after withdrawal
Initialization status is inferred from `if (startTime == 0)` even though startTime being 0 could later be intentionally reset or represent a valid unset-but-active state
